paragraphs: GovSpend sells public sector market intelligence to the companies that sell to government and to the agencies that buy. For sellers, the pitch is visibility before a solicitation is published, covering what agencies are buying, what they pay, who holds the work and when contracts renew. Agencies and school districts use the same data to see what comparable agencies paid and which vendors are competitive.

Purchasing data is gathered through relationships with agencies and handled by staff the company describes as data stewards, acquisition specialists, data engineers and software developers using patented technology. On the federal side, the Fedmine platform brings together 19 federal datasets in one place. Delivery options listed include single sign-on, a Slack app, CRM integrations, API access and an MCP server. The company says that MCP server puts 15 years of government procurement data inside common AI assistants and existing workflows.

Federal contracting information on the site is published with a GSA contract number. Contact details give an address in Boca Raton, Florida. The events list shows the company exhibiting at conferences, including one in Denver, Colorado.
